continuity.campaign_development: December 60 BCE: Valerius continued deeper into bandit-controlled country using captured watching-post records, but the older intelligence had to be tested against an adapting network. A false route and unreliable local information imposed delay and strain, while a concealed packet of newer records exposed changes in communications and dispersed supply. The expedition recovered usable provisions and entered the next phase with a substantially richer operational intelligence picture, while avoiding a pitched battle.

records.name: Principal estate

The component allocation is reconstructed here at 3.00 sq mi because the campaign descriptors consistently distinguish the principal estate as the primary landed/agricultural holding from the smaller lake-port commercial holding. This is a spatial reconstruction of the pre-existing 4.00 sq mi footprint, not a new acquisition.

The component allocation is reconstructed here at 1.00 sq mi because the campaign descriptors distinguish the lake port as a commercial/port node rather than the principal landed estate. This is a spatial reconstruction of the pre-existing 4.00 sq mi footprint, not a new acquisition.
